outcome: The Riemann Hypothesis itself (do all nontrivial zeta zeros lie on the critical line) remains fully open. The tracked partial-progress quantity — the best unconditional lower bound on the proportion of nontrivial zeros known to lie on the critical line — was moved from 41.6%/41.7% (Bui-Milinovich-Pratt-Zaharescu-type results from 2020) to over 67.2% by an unreleased Anthropic Claude research model in August 2026, subsequently reproduced with an independent, simpler proof by Youness Lamzouri (arXiv:2609.02882, Sept 2026). Numerous other 2024-2026 preprints claim full proofs or disproofs of RH; none show any sign of community acceptance.

ai.disclosed_cost: Anthropic's own account of the run (per secondary reporting, not independently confirmed by me from a primary Anthropic source beyond the research page) describes roughly 31 million output tokens across two sessions, about 60 subagents, 2,400 shell commands, and 54 arXiv papers reviewed.
systems: an internal research version of Claude

summary: The Riemann Hypothesis as stated in this bullet — do all nontrivial zeros of zeta lie on the critical line — is unchanged and remains open; per §3.1 an existence/universal-statement question of this kind moves only when fully answered, and nothing in the window answers it. What did happen is a genuine, well-documented movement of a *tracked partial quantity*: the best known unconditional lower bound on the proportion of nontrivial zeros proved to lie on the critical line (and be simple). This bound stood at roughly 41.6%-41.7% since around 2020 (Bui-Milinovich-Pratt-Zaharescu-type work referenced by both Anthropic and Lamzouri) and was raised to over 67.2% in a paper produced, by the authors' own account, by an unreleased internal research version of Claude in July-August 2026, announced by Anthropic on 2026-08-10 (https://www.anthropic.com/research/riemann-zeta). The proof was reviewed by two Anthropic mathematicians (Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman) and, per secondary reporting, examined favorably by external experts Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston; Claude also produced a Lean formalization of the key result with help from Anthropic's Eric Easley, which passed the Lean checker. This human-checked, AI-produced mathematics is what the `ai_role: bound` code is for: an AI system moved a bound on a problem (the proportion of zeros) that is still open, without the underlying Riemann Hypothesis itself being settled. I coded `ai_role` as `bound` rather than `generated` because the improved quantity is a partial/auxiliary result about the problem, not a resolution or counterexample to RH itself — `generated` and `assisted` describe roles in producing 'the mathematics that is in the result' for the problem as stated, and here the relevant 'result' for the RH bullet is null (no change). The Anthropic paper itself (title reported as 'More than two thirds of the zeros lie on the critical line') was not, as far as I could determine, submitted to or accepted by a journal as of my research (the PDF at the Anthropic CDN link was unreadable as raw text via WebFetch, so I relied on the arXiv record of Lamzouri's independent paper and secondary press coverage that quotes it directly). Lamzouri's independent, human-authored paper (arXiv:2609.02882, submitted 2026-09-02) reproduces and slightly extends the same bound (>67.25% simple-and-on-the-line, >83.62% distinct) with a different, Hilbert-space-based proof, explicitly crediting Claude's earlier result and its verification by Alpöge and Furman in its own text — this is the strongest primary-source confirmation I have of the AI claim, since it is a human mathematician's own written acknowledgement rather than only a press release. Separately, I checked several 2024-2026 preprints claiming to fully prove or disprove RH (e.g. arXiv:2404.06306 'Disproof of the Riemann Hypothesis', posted in math.GM — a non-refereed arXiv category — with three revisions through January 2025 and no evidence of acceptance or expert engagement; and other Zenodo/journal-mill postings such as the 'Most Definitive and Comprehensive Disproof Ever Constructed' piece). None of these show any sign of community acceptance, so they do not change the status. I did not find any withdrawal of the Claude/Anthropic bound result, so this is not coded as `incident`.
competing_reading: One could argue this deserves `status: open` with `no_change_found: true`, treating the 41.6%→67.2% bound movement as beside the stated RH question entirely (a 'related quantity', not even a restriction/case of it, since 'the proportion of zeros on the line' is not itself the yes/no question posed). I chose `progress` instead because the rubric explicitly lists 'a bound that moved' as counting, and separately defines `ai_role: bound` for exactly 'an AI system moved a bound on a problem that is still open' — implying the intended reading is that such bound movements on RH's tracked quantities are in scope as `progress` events even though they don't touch the yes/no question itself. If a stricter reading is preferred, this record should be `open`/`no_change_found: true` with the same AI material moved into `summary` only.
what_would_settle_it: Whether Anthropic's own paper (or a version of it) is submitted to and accepted by a journal or given a public expert digestion beyond the two internal mathematicians and two informally-consulted external readers; and whether the rubric's own maintainers intend 'a bound that moved' to include proportion-of-zeros results on RH specifically, versus reserving `progress`/`bound` for bounds that are themselves the stated question (per §3.1's constant/record-table carve-out).

events.credibility_reason: F5: landmark problem, no expert uptake, non-refereed math.GM category and repository postings, later work (Lamzouri 2026, Connes survey) still treats RH as open.

judgement.doubts: A bound on the proportion of zeros on the line counts as a bound on this bullet, so progress is right. Lamzouri's human proof is a bound at the same tier; the record says it 'reproduces and slightly extends' the result (67.25% vs >67.2%), which may just be the same bound stated to more digits. I did not treat it as superseding the AI bound: Lamzouri credits Claude's result as coming first. Even if it were read as superseding, the status would stay progress. The Anthropic PDF was never opened, and external endorsement by Conrey and Goldston rests on secondary reporting only.
